title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Risk-off tape; bonds, oil, and crypto stretched, semis broke.  
Equities bled all week as rising long-end yields and costly energy dominated; healthcare and metals absorbed flows while tech, utilities, and transports unwound. By Friday, calmer bonds and strong flash PMI at 56.8 staged a partial rebound, but indexes still closed lower across the board. The week’s arc: defensives and real assets bid, AI-hardware leadership cracked.

INDICES — Ranked WTD: DIA -0.85%, SPY -1.37%, IWM -1.68%, QQQ -2.41%. Small caps lagged large by 0.31pp per STYLE. VIX fell to 15.1, below its 20-day of 16.0. Most notable cross-asset move: SLV +7.25% WTD, with GLD +5.45%; TLT -0.35% on Friday, but 10-year yields near 4.7% all week. No index sits below its 200-day.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLV +4.33%, XLE +2.79%, XLB +1.90%, XLP -0.12%, XLY -0.15%, XLRE -0.42%, XLF -1.17%, XLC -1.37%, XLI -3.36%, XLU -3.48%, XLK -3.53%. Top industries: IBIT +22.59%, GDX +14.29%; bottom: ITA -6.27%, JETS -6.31%. Money rotated out of semis, utilities, and transports into healthcare, energy, and metals; crypto and gold absorbed the flows. Rotation label: AI hardware fading / high-to-low rotation.

DRIVERS — Semis led the decline, SOXX -5.52% WTD with negative 20d, while healthcare XLV +4.33% and energy XLE +2.79% absorbed flows; silver SLV +7.25% and gold GLD +5.45% were the week’s standout bids. Utilities XLU -3.48% unwound power/data-center bets on 3.8x vol spike in TAN, and transports JETS -6.31% cracked. No specific news catalyst explained the move; the mechanical driver was persistent elevated yields and oil near $93 Brent forcing rotation out of rate-sensitive long-duration tech.

WHAT'S NEXT — Watch whether QQQ’s pullback to -2.41% WTD finds support near maxpain 714, with skew at +5.1% suggesting downside hedging. Silver SLV 20d +19.26% with negative skew -5.4% is at an inflection—extended but with call interest flipping at 60.5. VIX 15.1 below its 20-day hints complacency; a break above 16.0 would confirm the risk-off regime persists into the September 16 FOMC.
